A.explanation: Net force is zero because the two $3.0\ \text{N}$ forces are opposite, but their moments about the pivot act in the same rotational sense so torque is not zero.

B.explanation: This is the moment of only one jet about the pivot, $3.0 \times 0.075 = 0.225\ \text{N m}$, and misses the equal contribution from the jet at the other end.

C.explanation: The two equal, opposite, perpendicular forces form a couple of separation $0.15\ \text{m}$, giving torque $3.0 \times 0.15 = 0.45\ \text{N m}$.

D.explanation: This doubles the couple result, $2 \times 3.0 \times 0.15 = 0.90\ \text{N m}$, by adding the separation twice instead of using torque $= F \times d$ once.

hints: Notice the tube is $0.15\ \text{m}$ long and pivoted in the middle, with a $3.0\ \text{N}$ force at right angles at each end in opposite directions.
Opposite forces at the two ends form a couple, so their moments about the pivot turn the tube the same way and must be added, not cancelled.
Calculate the couple as one force times the full separation between the forces, $F \times 0.15\ \text{m}$, and check the unit $\text{N m}$.
walkthrough: Identify the given data: each end has $F = 3.0\ \text{N}$ at $90^{\circ}$ to the tube, and the distance between the two lines of action is the full tube length $d = 0.15\ \text{m}$.
State the rule: torque $= F \times$ perpendicular distance from pivot, and for two opposite forces forming a couple, total torque $= F \times$ separation of the forces.
Check direction: viewed from above, both water jets push to rotate the tube the same way, so the two moments add.
Substitute with units: $3.0\ \text{N} \times 0.15\ \text{m} = 0.45\ \text{N m}$, which is also $2 \times (3.0 \times 0.075)$ for the two ends.
This magnitude matches $0.45\ \text{N m}$. This is option C.
